newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says to increase food rations from April.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says to increase food rations from April.

text.p: BAGHDAD, March 31 (Rueter) - Iraq said on Monday it would increase from April the monthly food rations handed out to Iraqis after the first shipments of food arrived in the country under an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

A spokesman for the Trade Ministry told the Iraqi News Agency the monthly flour quota per person would be raised from seven kilos (15.4 lb) to nine kilos (20 lb) from April while other items like sugar, rice, tea, cooking oil, pulses and detergents would be increased from May.
Most Iraqis have been suffering badly from shortages of food and medicine in a country under stringent U.N. sanctions imposed after its troops invaded Kuwait in 1990.
"It has been decided that as from April nine kilos of floor will be distributed for each individual as the first step of the new food rations under the memorandum (oil deal)," the spokesman said.

Iraqi and U.N. officials had announced that according to the new food rations each Iraqi would be entitled to nine kilos of flour instead of seven, 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) of rice instead of 1.25 kg (2.75 lb) and two kg (4.4 lb) of sugar instead of 750 grams (1.6 lb). Baby formula, tea and soap rations also go up.
Under the deal, which went into effect in December, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy urgent needs of its population.

The spokesman said a ship carrying 37,240 tonnes of wheat docked at Umm Qasr port on Monday, one of 14 other vessels that would anchor in the port during the next few days. He did not say whether the other shiploads were wheat or other foodstuffs.
The first shipment of food under the deal arrived last week, three months after implementation of the oil pact. Iraq blamed the United States for the delay and had complained to the United Nations.

"We were aiming to hand out all items of the new food rations under the memorandum of understanding as from the beginning of March but obstacles put by the American administration...have caused this delay," the spokesman said.
He said the arrived amount of wheat was not enough to cover the increase in flour ration but the ministry would use up to 40,000 tonnes from its stock.
The United Nations has deployed more than 100 observers to ensure the supplies are fairly distributed.
